nodes.title: the Vintfex signature
nodes.statement: The Vintfex system concerns objects called shenopals. There are exactly 5 of them: opallorn, qenthra, grixlum, vorpon, pontu. Two operations are written % and &. One relation is written ::, read as "yields to".

nodes.title: the Vintfex combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x % y for every pair of shenopals is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for &. The pairs standing in the :: relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all shenopals x and y, x % y is again a shenopal.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all shenopals x and y, x & y is again a shenopal.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all shenopals x, y, z: (x & y) & z = x & (y & z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all shenopals x and y: x & y = y & x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a shenopal opallorn with opallorn & x = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every shenopal x: x & x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every shenopal x: x :: x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all shenopals x and y: if x :: y and y :: x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all shenopals x, y, z: if x :: y and y :: z then x :: z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all shenopals x and y, at least one of x :: y and y :: x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all shenopals x, y, z: if x :: y then (z & x) :: (z & y) and (x & z) :: (y & z).

nodes.title: the system does not have association of the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all shenopals x, y, z: (x % y) % z = x % (y % z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = qenthra, y = opallorn, z = qenthra, left = opallorn, right = qenthra, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: grixka shenopals
nodes.statement: A shenopal x is called grixka when x % x = x.

nodes.title: shenopals that gelwren
nodes.statement: Two shenopals x and y are said to gelwren when x % y = y % x.

nodes.title: quilglim collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of shenopals is quilglim when x % y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the muxsib of a shenopal
nodes.statement: The muxsib of a shenopal x is the collection of shenopals y for which x :: y holds.

nodes.title: the shengel
nodes.statement: The shengel of the system is the collection of shenopals that gelwren with every shenopal.

nodes.title: the espanak
nodes.statement: The espanak is the collection of all grixka shenopals.

nodes.title: the thrafex of a shenopal
nodes.statement: The thrafex of a shenopal x, written [x], is the smallest quilglim collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a drisol
nodes.statement: A shenopal f is a drisol when f :: y holds for every shenopal y, that is, when the muxsib of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: the duthfal of a shenopal
nodes.statement: The duthfal of a shenopal x is the number of shenopals in its thrafex [x].

nodes.title: the tarnvor
nodes.statement: The tarnvor of the system is the collection of shenopals whose duthfal is largest.

nodes.title: aztgel pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct shenopals x and y form a aztgel pair when x :: y and y :: x both hold, that is, when each lies in the muxsib of the other.

nodes.title: the thrafex of a shenopal is quilglim
nodes.statement: For every shenopal x, the collection [x] is quilglim.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under %.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the thrafex is contained in every quilglim collection
nodes.statement: If S is quilglim and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a shenopal is grixka exactly when its duthfal is one
nodes.statement: x % x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x % x = x then {x} is already closed under %.
So [x] = {x} and the duthfal is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x % x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the duthfal divides the number of shenopals breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every shenopal x, the duthfal of x divides 5.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = qenthra, reach = 2, size = 5, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the espanak is quilglim
nodes.statement: If x and y are both grixka then so is x % y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be grixka.
The claim asks whether (x % y) % (x % y) returns x % y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: muxsibs are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the muxsib of x, then the muxsib of y is contained in the muxsib of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x :: y and let z satisfy y :: z.
Transitivity gives x :: z.
So every member of the muxsib of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one drisol
nodes.statement: No two distinct shenopals can both be drisols.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f :: h, since h is any object, and h :: f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a drisol
nodes.statement: Some shenopal drisols the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: no aztgel pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct shenopals lie in each other's muxsib.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.
